items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I think the A&R man was David something, I'm not sure.

ctx.x: So I have to go get a small band because they will pay for a small band, and maybe get a vocal in there and some sort of entertainment. And this is what I'm doing continuously. And with ups and downs. And meanwhile, I get a date from Mercury, the Hot Fivers, they gave me that date. And that's through an agent, again. He was able to maneuver a date. And this is -- it gives you a little picture of what the music business is like.

One of the tunes I decided to record, of course, is 'Grandpa Spells.' And I think the A&R man was David something, I'm not sure. But he was also a pianist, had his own band. Anyway, I recorded this record and 'Sweet Georgia Brown' and other things. And for those times -- and it still is a good
record, for what it started out to be. It's concise, it's more like a John Kirby band.
